caption: The Gran Teatro Falla, named after composer Manuel de Falla, is the main venue for Cádiz's yearly Carnival singing-group competitions.

landmark: Barrio Sur and Palermo, candombe neighborhoods
caption: In Montevideo's Sur and Palermo neighborhoods, drum groups play candombe in street processions; UNESCO added the tradition to its intangible heritage list in 2009.
Estadio Tetelo Vargas is the home ballpark of the Estrellas Orientales in San Pedro de Macorís, a city known for producing many professional baseball players.
The Yungas Road links La Paz with Bolivia's Yungas region, and in 1995 the Inter-American Development Bank called it the most dangerous road in the world.
Joya de Cerén was a farming village buried by a volcanic eruption around AD 600, and it is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The town of Yanga, Veracruz, began as a settlement of escaped enslaved people and was renamed in 1932 after its leader, Gaspar Yanga.
Construction of the Palacio de los López in Asunción began in 1857, and the neoclassical building now serves as the seat of Paraguay's government.

landmark: Cultural space of Palenque de San Basilio
caption: San Basilio de Palenque, southeast of Cartagena, is home to the Palenquero creole language, and UNESCO lists its cultural space as intangible heritage.
Elogio del Horizonte, a 10-metre concrete sculpture by Eduardo Chillida, stands on a cliff in Gijón overlooking the Cantabrian Sea and was inaugurated in 1990.
Hacienda San José, near El Carmen in the Chincha province, was a sugar plantation worked by enslaved people and now operates as a hotel.
